title: Hue Amazing Marathon 2026 Review: Imperial City Debut From a Proven Vietnam Series
seo_title: Hue Amazing Marathon 2026 Review | Vietnam Race
meta_description: Hue Amazing Marathon 2026 review: August 30 in Hue, Vietnam -- four distances from a Bolt Event series praised at its sister race in Quang Tri.
dek: Set for 29-30 August 2026 (race day the 30th) in Vietnam's former imperial capital, this debut Hue leg of Bolt Event's Amazing Marathon Vietnam Series follows a sister race in Quang Tri that drew praise for its organisation and scenery.
verdict: The Hue Amazing Marathon is a new addition to Bolt Event's Amazing Marathon Vietnam Series, run by the same organiser behind the Aqua Warriors Vietnam Series and the Quang Tri Amazing Marathon since 2024. Four distances from 5km to the full 42km give it broad appeal, set against Hue's backdrop as Vietnam's former imperial capital under the Nguyen dynasty. There's no participant feedback for Hue specifically since the race hasn't happened yet, but the sister Quang Tri event earlier in the same 2026 series drew genuine runner praise for its organisation, route safety support and scenery -- a reasonable proxy for what to expect operationally, even if the Hue course itself is unproven.

sections.heading: A New Leg in a Growing Vietnam Series
paragraphs: Hue Amazing Marathon 2026 is scheduled for 29-30 August 2026, with race day on the 30th, offering four distances: 5km, 10km, 21km and 42km. [1] The event is part of Bolt Event's 'Amazing Marathon Vietnam Series,' the same organiser that also runs the Aqua Warriors Vietnam Series (Ha Long, Van Don, Quang Tri, Hue) since 2024 and the Quang Tri Amazing Marathon.

sections.heading: What the Sister Race Tells Us
paragraphs: There's no participant feedback specific to the Hue race since it hasn't taken place yet, but the Quang Tri Amazing Marathon 2026 -- held earlier in the same series, same organiser -- drew genuine praise. One runner quoted in Tien Phong's coverage said of the event: "Chay giai nay vua chill vua suong, canh dep qua, binh minh tren bien dep qua" (roughly: this race is both relaxing and satisfying, the scenery and sea sunrise are beautiful). [2] That's a reasonable signal for organisational and scenic standards across the series, even if it doesn't confirm Hue's specific course.

sections.heading: Hue: Vietnam's Former Imperial Capital
paragraphs: Hue served as the capital of Vietnam under the Nguyen dynasty from 1802 to 1945 and later as the administrative capital of the French protectorate of Annam, with a population of roughly 653,000 as of 2020. [3] The city's Imperial City -- walled courtyards, gardens, pavilions and palaces -- gives race weekend a genuine cultural draw well beyond the course itself.

sections.heading: Cut-Offs and Pricing
paragraphs: Group-registration cut-off times are listed as 1h15 for 5km, 2h for 10km, 3h30 for 21km, and 6h30 for 42km. [1] Early-bird pricing (13-19 July window) was listed at roughly VND 559,000 for the 42km, VND 489,000 for the 21km, and VND 379,000 for the 5-10km categories.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you're drawn to running through Vietnam's former imperial capital and trust an organiser with a track record of well-received races elsewhere in the same series, the Hue Amazing Marathon on 30 August 2026 is a reasonable bet. Just know that no Hue-specific reviews exist yet -- the praise on file so far comes from the sister Quang Tri race, not this course.
